newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S. African oil row motions withdrawn in parliament.
newsitem.headline: S. African oil row motions withdrawn in parliament.

text.p: A potentially explosive debate in parliament about the increasingly acrimonious public row between South African Minerals and Energy Minister Penuell Maduna and Auditor-General Henri Kleuver was averted on Tuesday.

After much argument and counter-argument, a National Party motion asking for the appointment of a judicial commission of inquiry into Maduna's recent allegations that Kleuver had helped cover up the theft of 170 million rand from the state's Strategic Fuel Fund was withdrawn.
As a result, an African National Congress amendment asking the Public Protector to investigate the row and Maduna's conduct was also withdrawn.

The National Party withdrew its motion following the release of a resolution by the powerful audit commission on Monday which said it expected the parliamentary public accounts committee to examine the allegations and counter-allegations as part of its normal review of the work of the Auditor-General.
The commission, a statutory body which oversees the work of the Auditor-General, said that it planned to ask President Nelson Mandela to help end exchanges between the two in the media.
"(This is) damaging to the important principle of support and assistance between the various organs and institutions of state," it said.
